newsitem.title: USA: Payless Cashways debt sees lengthy decline.
newsitem.headline: Payless Cashways debt sees lengthy decline.

text.p: Bonds of Payless Cashways Inc continued to deteriorate, losing another 3-1/2 points this week, bringing the total decline since last month to slightly over 25 points, high-yield bond traders said.
The firm's 9-1/8 percent bonds have withstood a precipitous drop from the low 50's area where they initially traded in early June, players said.
"These bonds have deteriorated dramatically over the last month," said one high-yield trader. "I don't think these bonds have anywhere to go but down."
Currently, the debt is trading at a 23-1/2 bid, 24-1/2 offer, junk traders said.
The company could not immediately be reached for comment.

The Kansas City-based specialty retailer's bonds came under pressure following disappointing second quarter operating results, a debt restructuring announcement, and downgrades to the firm's credit ratings.
In its June 17 release, the company said that while it continued to have adequate liquidity and remained in compliance with bank loan covenants, it had scheduled discussions with bank lenders.
Prior to its restructuring annoucement, the company reported a loss for the second quarter ended May 31 of $0.37 a share, compared with a year-ago profit of $0.11.
"A balance sheet restructuring we think is the most likely scenario," said Clare Schiedermayer, high-yield retail analyst with Merrill Lynch & Co Inc.
"Most people are not overly confident though that they will be able to come to an agreement with the banks that does not also require dealing with the subordinated debt," Schiedermayer said.
Analysts said the market was pricing in the risk that subordinated debt was not very well off in the restructuring scenario, as senior debt is positioned ahead of the company's other bonds.
"They are talking a restructuring deal which could make those bonds worth between 12 and 15," said another trader. "I have not seen a real buyer in these bonds in the last two months."

Last month, both Moody's Investors Service Inc and Standard & Poor's cut Payless' credit ratings, citing continued deterioration in the company's operating performance coupled with its recent announcement of negotiations with its bank group to restructure its credit facilities.
The agencies also pointed to intense competition, specifically, from other specialty retailers such as Home Depot Inc and Lowes Cos Inc, which continued to gain market share.
Payless Cashways secured bank loan is rated B-minus by S&P. The firm's subordinated debt is rated CCC by S&P.
Moody's rates the company's senior secured bank facility at B2, the senior secured bank facility at B1 and the firm's senior subordinated notes at Caa1.
Payless Cashways operates 193 building centers in 22 states across the Midwestern, Southwestern, Pacific Coast, Rocky Mountain, and New England areas.
